README: AI-era cyber training catalogue — draft v7
Built on the Capability Model (levels and needs) and the Practices Playbook. 5 Oct 2026. Assumptions marked 'to validate' in the work plan are treated as correct.
How it is organised
Scoring guide — the 0 to 3 scale, the band rules and the two thresholds (yellow cells) that set them.
Needs — the 14 core needs and 9 role extras of the Capability Model, one row each, with how far the catalogue covers each. Set Status to Retired rather than deleting, so past scores still resolve.

Rubric — every need broken into the requirements a training must cover, one row each, with stable Req IDs (N2.6, R1.1.3) and a Core flag for must-haves. Add a requirement by typing in the row under the table; formulas fill in by themselves.
Scores — one row per training and requirement assessed: Offer ID, Req ID, a score from 0 to 3, and where in the course the evidence is.
Coverage — one row per training and need: enter Offer ID, Need code and the level the training targets; coverage %, Core gaps and the band are worked out from Scores.

Paths — two to five trainings combined for one need. Each requirement takes the best score any of them reached; 'Below 3' is the build list. Path detail shows the result requirement by requirement (first 40 paths).

Matrix — one row per level and need: the base for everyone, the templates for Entry, Practitioner and Expert (roles 1-7), and the extras for each macro role. Each row lists the proposed training, any build item, and the practices (PR codes) used to practise and prove it. Not yet rebuilt on the 14 needs of the Needs sheet: it still uses the earlier need codes.

Offers — the training that works on any tool stack, with stable IDs: TR-### for external offers, INT-### for the bank's internal Udemy Business courses (ID cells shaded green). 'Used in matrix rows' shows where each is proposed.

Tool track — training tied to one product. It is used only when the product is adopted; 'Wave' comes from the Tool adoption sheet (A13). INT-B## rows are the bank's internal Udemy Business courses (ID cells shaded green).
Tool adoption — the draft adoption waves from A13. Edit the yellow cells as the roadmap (I3) firms up.
Build items — what we must create in-house because the market and existing training don't cover it.
Codes — the level, need and practice codes.
Screening log — every offer from the external research list of 5 Oct 2026 and what was done with it.
How to review

Domain heads review the Matrix rows for their role; the Group CISO reviews the base rows and role 8. Set 'Review status' to Confirmed or Rejected and add a comment. Rejected training goes back to the gap list.
The same 'Review status' column on Offers records the decision on each individual training.

How to score a training
1. Add a Coverage row for each need the training claims to address (the course outline, or Offers 'Needs (assessed)'), with the level it targets.

2. In Scores, score every in-scope requirement of that need from 0 to 3 using the Scoring guide, and say where the evidence is. Unscored requirements count as 0, so 'Scored' against 'In scope' shows when an assessment is complete.
3. Read the band. Full means every requirement at 3; Strong means coverage at or above the Strong minimum with no Core requirement at 0; Partial and Weak follow the thresholds on the Scoring guide.
4. Where no single training reaches Strong, combine two to five in Paths. What the best path still leaves below 3 becomes a build item.
Keeping the rubric current

Change wording in place and update 'Last changed'. Never reuse a Req ID for a different requirement: retire the old one and add a new ID (for example N8.6), so recorded scores keep their meaning. Duplicate Req IDs, and duplicate training-requirement pairs in Scores, are shaded red. New needs go in Needs first; the Need code lists read from it. Raise the thresholds on the Scoring guide as the market matures.
Changes from v6 (13 Oct 2026)

All 308 trainings in Offers were desk-reviewed against the rubric: the provider page (for the bank's Udemy Business courses, the same course on public udemy.com), plus the official syllabus or outline where the page was thin. 260 had a full syllabus, 46 a description only, 2 could not be found (TR-017, TR-045). Each training was scored 0 to 3 on every in-scope requirement of each need where at least one requirement reached 2: 772 training-need rows in Coverage and 4,963 scores in Scores, each with an evidence note. Scores rest on syllabi, not on taking the courses, and are conservative: a lecture title alone gets at most 2, and a 3 on a skill needs a visible lab or exercise. Offers now shows, per training, the evidence level, a content summary, the coverage at assessment, a fit note and the sources; 'Needs (draft tags)' became 'Needs (assessed)', Best-fit level and Teaches supervision were reset from the review, and the 174 internal courses moved from 'To assess' to 'Assessed'. Reviewer decisions (Proposed, Not proposed) were left unchanged.
Changes from v4 (13 Oct 2026)

Added Scoring guide, Needs, Rubric, Scores, Coverage, Paths and Path detail. The Rubric breaks the Capability Model (doc revision 288) into 140 requirements: 90 for the 14 core needs and 50 for the 9 role extras. Role-extra requirements are the model's numbered items, unchanged; core-need requirements split its prose into one row per item it names. 55 requirements are flagged Core as a first proposal for the domain heads to confirm. Scoring is a gradient (0 to 3, coverage %, four bands) rather than full or partial; the Capability Model's matching rule was updated to match. Codes now points to the Needs sheet, and its level definitions drop the autonomy ladder removed from the model.

Run incidents where the agent is the subject

The ways to stop an agent and when to use each: revoke its identity or session token so it can no longer call any tool; disable only the tools or connectors it misuses while the rest keeps running; put it in observe-only mode, where it may analyse and recommend but is barred from acting; roll back what it changed using its action log
Run incidents where the agent is the subject

Where the attack comes from: content the agent reads (logs, alerts, tickets, documents, emails, web pages) can carry instructions aimed at it, so the investigator looks for injection in those sources and cuts any that is poisoned. Solid, widely used RMF explainer for GRC and BISO staff starting N13; it is knowledge-only (no exercises), lightly agentic, and overlaps TR-118.

Thin generic business content (about 2-3 min per lecture, partly AI-generated). INT-2478 covers the same ground with better practice and is newer, so keep INT-2478 and drop this one.
Organizational Redesign in the AI Era

Course (GenMan Solutions) for leaders and transformation staff on how organisations should change when AI joins the workforce. Exercises include a graded-by-answer-key task sort, a spreadsheet metrics dashboard on a claims-processing scenario, role plays and a 90-day/12-month roadmap workbook.

The better of the two same-title courses (newer, real exercises). It is a reasonable generic primer for leaders and champions on N14 work redesign and measuring value, but it isn't cyber-specific and doesn't cover supervision design.
